Analysis: Both hypotheses propose innovative dual strategies that integrate metabolic reprogramming with immune modulation in HCC. Hypothesis 1 innovatively combines tumor-specific MAT inhibition with chemokine axis blockade, leveraging established technologies (e.g., CRISPR-Cas9, single-cell transcriptomics) in a dual-intervention framework. It presents a clearer, though still complex, set of mechanistic links that can be individually validated in vitro and in vivo. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 employs a dual-modulation approach that involves both suppression (via CRISPR/dCas9) and activation (via microRNA) of distinct MAT enzymes, delivered via liver-tropic nanoparticles. While highly novel, Hypothesis 2 faces significant challenges in terms of the integration and safety of these multi-modal delivery systems, as well as in clearly delineating the precise causal cascade linking metabolic changes and immune checkpoint modulation. Therefore, Hypothesis 1 is superior in terms of overall plausibility and testability, and its safety concerns appear somewhat more manageable due to the more discrete nature of the interventions.
